text: Today we have a question from a lady. Seems like her boyfriend has some trust issues and wants to check her phone all the time. By the way, only about 15% of my viewers are women, so I appreciate that despite my content being mostly for men, some of you ladies watch it and even ask questions. So let's go to the question from Lana. Remember that joke from some movie. How to better remember Lana? Just read it backwards. Hello Ilyas, I don't know if you will see this, but I have a question. I just ended my one year relationship with my boyfriend over something small. What was so small there that you ended your relationship with your boyfriend? For context, I have been with my boyfriend for one year and we trust each other fully. Location, always on, and we know each other's phone passwords, but even though we trust each other, I don't feel like he trusts me fully. I think this is because I don't like giving my phone out to other people, even if I have nothing to hide. I don't think in a relationship you're obligated to give your phone whenever your partner asks for it, not because I'm cheating or hiding something. Yeah, come on Lana, where are the commas, where the punctuation? I snap on the guys when they send me questions and they can't even formulate their thoughts, but similar problem here. I don't think in a relationship you're obligated to give your phone whenever your partner asks for it, not because I'm cheating or hiding something, because I know I'm not. Just because I don't like people snooping through my stuff and my phone, I think my boyfriend feels like I might be hiding something. It's still one sentence, but I just don't like giving my phone out because of privacy and stuff. Don't get me wrong, I'll give it to him if he has a good reason or because his phone died and I don't feel nervous about it, but when he asks to just check my phone, I do sometimes give it. I'm just scared that he will find something, even though there is nothing there. I just don't feel good when someone does that. So if you see this, could you please give me some tips and maybe also your opinion on this. Thank you so much and I absolutely love your videos, by the way. Okay, thank you Lana for your nice words and for your question, but I think it goes for both men and women. Guys, until you learn how to formulate your thoughts, how to construct your sentences, how to use punctuation, don't do relationships. Learn how to write first. Now to the question, is trust important in a relationship? Yes, it is. Guys, if you are in a relationship where you constantly feel that you need to check your partner's phone to make sure she or he is faithful to you, what kind of relationship is that? If your partner is not giving you any good reasons for that, but you still want to do it all the time, something is wrong with you and it is completely normal that your partner would freak out. If there are reasons, there are actions of your partner that make you question her or his behavior, then why do you even need to check the phone? Actions can already tell you enough. But okay, if for your peace of mind you checked her phone and found out something, that's it. Break up. What's the point of checking it again and again? So answering your question, Lana, yes, it was the right decision to break up with your boyfriend. If what you are saying is true, you didn't give much reasons for him to doubt you and he was just paranoid and checked your phone again and again, that is a weird guy and it's the right decision to break up with him. So I hope you will learn how to better formulate your thoughts and eventually find a good guy who maybe also watch my channel. Thanks a lot. My name is Ilyas Abdullin and bye!
